Cluster Bootstrap of a Linear Mixed-Effects Model

Source: R/boot_lmer.R
boot_lmer.Rd

Refits a linear mixed model ([lme4::lmer()]) on bootstrap resamples of whole groups (for example subjects), drops outlying bootstrap estimates of each fixed effect with Tukey's fences ([calculate_fences()]) and summarises what is left: mean, standard error, median, percentile interval and a two-tailed bootstrap p-value ([boot_p_value()]). It is the "resample, fit with a fallback, tidy, drop outlying coefficients, summarise" block that report templates otherwise repeat.

Usage

boot_lmer(
  formula,
  data,
  group,
  n_boot = 1000L,
  normalize = NULL,
  fence = c("outer", "inner", "none"),
  fallback_formula = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  include_intercept = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  parallel = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A mixed-model formula with a random-effect term, for example `y ~ x1 + x2 + (1 | id)`.

data

A data frame.

group

Name of the column that identifies the groups to resample (the grouping factor of the random effect; a warning is given when it is not one of the formula's grouping factors). Missing values are an error; unused factor levels are ignored.

n_boot

Number of bootstrap replicates (default 1000).

normalize

`NULL` or the names of numeric columns to rescale to \[0, 1\] within each resample.

fence

`"outer"` (default), `"inner"` or `"none"`; see Details.

fallback_formula

`NULL` or a formula used when the model fails.

conf_level

Confidence level of the percentile interval (default 0.95).

include_intercept

If `TRUE`, the intercept is summarised too (default `FALSE`).

seed

Optional integer. With it the result is reproducible, and the random number generator state of the session is restored afterwards.

parallel

If `TRUE`, the replicates are fitted with `furrr::future_map()` under the current future plan (set it with `future::plan()`, for example `future::plan("multisession")`; under the default sequential plan nothing runs in parallel). Default `FALSE`, the sequential loop. In parallel mode each replicate has its own random-number stream, so the result for a given `seed` is the same under any plan and any number of workers, but it is not the result of the sequential loop for that `seed`. `seed` must be a single number in this mode. The same version of TempleCBE must be installed on the workers (they load the installed package, not a `load_all()` source tree, and resolve its helper functions from it), and the arguments in `...` are evaluated before fitting (they cannot name columns of `data`, such as `weights = n`).

...

Passed to [lme4::lmer()].

Value

A tibble of class `boot_lmer`, one row per fixed effect: `term`, `n` (kept estimates), `mean`, `sd`, `std.error`, `median`, `lower`, `upper`, `p.value`. Attributes: `draws` (every bootstrap estimate: `boot`, `term`, `estimate`, `fallback`, `comparable`, `kept`), `n_boot`, `n_failed`, `n_fallback`, `n_incomparable`, `n_singular`, `n_nonconverged`, `fence`, `conf_level`.

Details

Each replicate draws as many groups as there are, with replacement, and uses all rows of every drawn group. A group drawn twice keeps its identifier, so it is still one level of the random effect (as with `rsample::group_bootstraps()`).

`normalize` names numeric columns that are rescaled to \[0, 1\] by their minimum and maximum within each resample ([min_max_norm()]) before the model is fitted, so the estimates are per full range of the predictor.

A replicate whose model cannot be fitted is refitted with `fallback_formula`, if one is given (for example the intercept-only `y ~ -1 + (1 | id)`); a fallback model contributes only the fixed effects it has, and those estimates come from another model than the rest (they are flagged `fallback` in `draws`). A replicate that cannot be fitted at all is counted in `n_failed` and contributes nothing. Warnings and messages from the fits are not shown; the number of singular and of non-converged fits is returned in `n_singular` and `n_nonconverged`.

Rank-deficient resamples. When a resample lacks a level of a factor (or a predictor is constant in it), `lme4` drops the columns it cannot estimate, and the remaining contrasts then mean something else (with level A absent, `fC` estimates C - B and not C - A). The columns of the model fitted to the whole data are the reference: a replicate whose columns differ is not comparable, contributes to no term and is counted in `n_incomparable`. A predictor named in `normalize` that is constant in a resample is mapped to 0 and dropped by `lme4` in the same way.

The fences are applied to the bootstrap estimates of each term separately: an estimate is kept when it lies strictly between the lower and upper fence (the inner fences at 1.5 x IQR, the outer at 3 x IQR); when the interquartile range is 0 the fences coincide with the bulk value and the bulk is kept, so that only the values off it are dropped. `fence = "none"` keeps every estimate.

`std.error` is the standard deviation of the kept estimates divided by the square root of their number. That is the Monte Carlo error of the bootstrap mean, not the standard error of the estimate (which is `sd`), and it shrinks as `n_boot` grows. It is kept because the report templates used it, and because the p-value uses it as the tolerance `epsilon` around the null value. Percentile limits use all kept estimates. Terms are returned in model order. A p-value of 0 means no kept estimate lay on the other side of the null; it is not exact (see [boot_p_value()]).

A group drawn twice keeps its identifier and so counts as one level of the random effect, which slightly inflates the random-effect variance; fixed effects are not affected in practice.

See also

[fit_lmer_safely()], [calculate_fences()], [boot_p_value()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
boot_lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), lme4::sleepstudy, group = "Subject",
          n_boot = 200, normalize = "Days", seed = 1)
} # }
